# Mirg

> Mirg is a desktop app for making video games with AI. You describe a game in plain words, typed or spoken, and an AI agent writes it, runs it, and plays it to check that it works. The game appears next to the chat, ready to play and change. Free to try on Mac.

## What it does

- Builds a game from a description, then keeps changing it as you ask: "add a double jump", "add an enemy", "generate real art for the fox".
- Runs the game and tests its own work: it takes screenshots, presses keys, taps the screen and reads the score, then fixes what is broken. It says what it could not check.
- Shows the game, the code and the art in three tabs. Projects are ordinary folders on your own computer.
- Every message has a Restore button, so any change can be undone.
- Offers Claude, GPT and Gemini models, with a control for how hard the model thinks. No API keys are needed.

## Platforms it builds for

Web, phone and Godot games play inside Mirg, where the agent can see and test them. Other engines work if they are installed, and Mirg shows what is missing and how to get it.

- Web games, 2D and 3D: nothing to install
- iPhone and Android: phone preview with touch, then a real app in the iOS Simulator or Android emulator
- Godot: Mirg can install it
- Unity
- Unreal Engine (C++ and engine templates)
- Roblox (built for you, played in Roblox Studio)
- Minecraft: Java Edition mods
- Ren'Py visual novels
- Python (pygame)
- LÖVE
- GameMaker (Mirg edits the code; you run it from GameMaker)

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple Silicon or Intel, macOS 12 or later. Windows and Linux versions are in the works.
- An email address to sign in. Nothing else to set up.

## Pricing

- Free: $0, enough usage for a handful of small games each month.
- Pro: $20 a month, 14 times the free plan's usage.
- Max: $100 a month, over 5 times Pro's usage, with the option to keep building when it runs out.

Plans can be cancelled at any time. Usage means the cost of the AI models running your requests; bigger games and more capable models use it faster.

## Platform guides

Each has a real example: the request, what the agent did, how long it took, and what is needed.

- [Make a web game with AI](https://mirg.ai/web-games): Describe a game and play it in about a minute. Web games need nothing installed, and they run inside Mirg, where the agent can see the screen, press the keys and read the score to check its own work.
- [Make an iPhone or Android game with AI](https://mirg.ai/iphone-android-games): Build a game with touch controls in a phone preview, then turn it into a real app that runs in the iOS Simulator or the Android emulator. The agent plays it with taps and swipes to check it.
- [Make a Godot game with AI](https://mirg.ai/godot): Describe a game and the agent writes a real Godot 4 project: scenes, scripts and settings. Godot games play inside Mirg, so the agent can see and test them, and Mirg can install Godot for you.
- [Make a Unity game with AI](https://mirg.ai/unity): Describe a game and the agent writes the C# scripts, builds the scene and compiles a playable Unity game. It opens in its own window, where the agent can look at it and play it.
- [Make an Unreal Engine game with AI](https://mirg.ai/unreal-engine): Describe a game and the agent sets up an Unreal project from the engine's own templates, builds the level with a script, and launches it. Unreal games open in their own window.
- [Make a Roblox game with AI](https://mirg.ai/roblox): Describe a Roblox game and the agent writes the Luau scripts, lays out the parts and builds a place file. It opens in Roblox Studio, where you press Play.
- [Make a Minecraft mod with AI](https://mirg.ai/minecraft-mods): Describe what you want added to Minecraft and the agent writes a real Java Edition mod, compiles it, and starts a test copy of the game with the mod loaded.
- [Make a Ren'Py visual novel with AI](https://mirg.ai/renpy): Describe a story and the agent writes a Ren'Py visual novel: the script, the characters, the choices and the endings. It runs Ren'Py's own checker, then opens the game.
- [Make a Python game with AI](https://mirg.ai/pygame): Describe a game and the agent writes it in Python with pygame, tests it without opening a window, and then runs it. A common first game, and a good way to learn from working code.
- [Make a LÖVE (Love2D) game with AI](https://mirg.ai/love2d): Describe a game and the agent writes it in Lua for LÖVE, checks the code, and starts it. Small, fast 2D games in a couple of files.
- [Change a GameMaker game with AI](https://mirg.ai/gamemaker): Open a GameMaker project in Mirg and ask for changes in plain words. The agent edits the GML code; you press Run in GameMaker to see them.
